review.why: Create, fill and restyle print-ready PDFs with a design system: 15 document types, charts, math, tables and form filling.
review.summary: Three routes: CREATE a styled PDF from a content file (cover rendered in a headless browser, body with ReportLab), FILL existing form fields after inspecting their names, and REFORMAT Markdown, text or PDF into the design. A design guide explains palette, type and spacing.
strengths: Complete pipeline with 20 block types (tables, charts, math, flowcharts, bibliography) and a documented design rationale.
Form filling inspects the real field names first instead of guessing them.
A check command reports missing dependencies, and the merge step runs a page-count and file-size sanity check.
cautions: Heavy setup: Python 3.9+ with reportlab and pypdf, Node 18+, Playwright and Chromium. Several scripts install missing packages themselves (pip with --break-system-packages, npm install -g).
Cover pages load Google Fonts over the network when rendered; body pages use system fonts.

SKILL.md, the design guide, make.sh, merge.py and render_cover.js were read; the large rendering scripts were searched for risky calls, not read line by line, and the pipeline was not run, so output quality is unverified.
